R-01.intendToFix: yes, before the first durable Account cutover.
R-01.importance: high cutover availability; medium current exposure.
R-01.assessment:
Confirmed on 6ba7c22 with synthetic service fixtures and the actual bundled receiver verifier: a 614,400-byte update is accepted and served as a 614,698-byte envelope, then verification refuses size. A 16 KiB fixture fits the wire limit; 4 MiB is refused by the service. This is an authenticated nonconforming-member/future-sender risk, not a demonstrated unauthenticated attack or loss of stored writing. Reopening repeats the blocking position; “permanent” means persistent for unchanged readers. The scheduler does retain generic operation-failed, while the useful inbound cause/diagnostic is lost.

Use a shared service-visible wire policy, sender pre-seal/count/decoded-byte checks, aligned codec/receiver counts and bounded terminal diagnostics. The service cannot inspect encrypted counts or Yjs validity; a size cap alone cannot guarantee progress against arbitrary malformed member ciphertext. Preserve refusal safety and existing ledger bytes, define recovery for an already accepted bad position, and test exact boundaries, unchanged accepted prefix on refusal, and cause visibility. Do not equate the 64 KiB batch policy with every single-source envelope. This is more than an isolated constant edit; R-01 stays distinct, with diagnostic overlap under F-10.
